question: A hemisphere of radius 5 cm is carved from a sphere. What is the volume of the hemisphere?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The volume of a hemisphere is exactly half the volume of a complete sphere.

Volume = (2/3) × π × r³

Substitute r = 5 cm directly into the formula.

Volume = (2/3) × π × 125 = 250π/3 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 250π/3 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the hemisphere (r) = 5 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a hemisphere = (2/3) × π × r³

 

 
 
 
• 
 r = 5 cm
 Hemisphere

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume = (2/3) × π × (5)³

⇒ Volume = (2/3) × π × 125

⇒ Volume = 250π/3 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 250π/3 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Full Sphere

The total volume of a complete sphere is given by V = (4/3) × π × r³. A hemisphere's volume is exactly half of this value.

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

The curved surface area of a hemisphere only accounts for the outer bowl part and is calculated as CSA = 2 × π × r².

Total Surface Area (TSA)

The total surface area includes both the curved surface and the flat circular top surface. It is calculated as TSA = 3 × π × r².
